steps.name: Project brief
steps.problem: A project starts without anyone writing down what it is, for whom, how long, and with what money.
steps.does: Pins the format, length, audience, platform, budget level and way of making it, then decides which steps this project needs and which to skip.

steps.name: Story
steps.problem: The story lives in one head. Everyone downstream works from a different version of it.
steps.does: Completes the story in the international development format: title, logline, characters, world, acts, beat sheet and a one-page synopsis.

steps.name: Screenplay
steps.problem: A story is not yet a plan. Until it is in scenes, nothing can be scheduled, costed or shot.
steps.does: Turns the story into a scene outline, then writes every scene in standard screenplay form, as a draft for the writer to rewrite.

steps.name: Script breakdown
steps.problem: A script is read by twelve departments, and each keeps its own list.
steps.does: Reads the script and drafts the film's record: people, costumes, props, places and light, and the scene where each first appears.

steps.name: Look and cast lock
steps.problem: Each tool and each vendor starts from its own picture of the character.
steps.does: Drafts one approved look for each face, costume and place, for generators and vendors to start from.

steps.name: Previs and shot plan
steps.problem: The shot list lives in one head and the storyboard in another.
steps.does: Turns the scene into a shot plan, and says which shots a camera should take and which a generator can.

steps.name: Budget
steps.problem: Money is guessed late and line by line, and the expensive scenes are found after they are scheduled.
steps.does: Builds a top sheet and line budget from the breakdown at the brief's budget level, and names the scenes that drive the cost.

steps.name: Schedule and risk
steps.problem: The fragile days are found on the day they break.
steps.does: Reads the schedule against cast dates, locations and weather, marks the days most likely to break, and holds a cover plan for each.

steps.name: Crew and locations
steps.problem: Crew and places are booked from memory, and the gaps appear on the first day.
steps.does: Lists the crew this project needs at its scale, and every location with what it must provide, permits and a backup.

steps.name: Tools and vendor plan
steps.problem: Tools are chosen shot by shot, and later nobody can say which made what.
steps.does: Sets which tool or vendor makes each shot. The tools already in use come first, then they are connected, and custom code comes last.

steps.name: Call sheets
steps.problem: Each night someone rebuilds tomorrow by hand from the schedule, the cast list and the weather.
steps.does: Turns the schedule into a call sheet for every shoot day: scenes, cast, calls, locations, special needs.

steps.name: Generated shots
steps.problem: Generated shots are made one prompt at a time, by different people, from different pictures of the character.
steps.does: Drafts the generation plan for each generated shot: the prompt, the reference it starts from, and what continuity it must hold.

steps.name: The day breaks
steps.problem: Rain stops the shoot. The unit waits, the day is lost, and the schedule is rebuilt by hand overnight.
steps.does: Re-solves the day against cast dates, locations and what is already shot, proposes a cover scene and drafts the new call sheet.

steps.name: On-set continuity
steps.problem: Costume and props drift between days. The script supervisor holds it all in notes and photos.
steps.does: Checks each setup against the film's record before the camera rolls.

steps.name: Coverage check
steps.problem: A missing angle is found at rushes the next day, after the unit has left the location.
steps.does: Checks the takes against the shot plan beside the set, and flags the gap before the unit moves.

steps.name: Location sound
steps.problem: Unusable location sound sends the scene to dubbing weeks later.
steps.does: Reads the sound report the same night and lists only the lines that cannot be saved.

steps.name: Rushes overnight
steps.problem: Rushes pile up. The director sees selects days later.
steps.does: Logs a day's takes by scene and take from your notes, and proposes a first assembly order.

steps.name: Edit assist
steps.problem: Finding the take with the right line eats the editor's day.
steps.does: Finds takes by what is said and done in them, and builds string-outs for the editor to cut from.

steps.name: Continuity check
steps.problem: A shot is regenerated by a second vendor. Nobody on that team has seen the rest of the film.
steps.does: Compares a new shot with what the film's record holds, shows each possible break beside the shot that set it, and leaves the decision to a person.

steps.name: Vendor turnover
steps.problem: Three vendors deliver the same character. Each one matches its own reference.
steps.does: Drafts each vendor's turnover note with the record entries it needs, and the checks the delivery should pass.

steps.name: Sound, music and dub
steps.problem: Every language version is rebuilt by hand, and lines drift from the picture.
steps.does: Keeps one list of lines across languages and marks where a dub no longer fits the cut.

steps.name: Colour grade
steps.problem: The look drifts from shot to shot, and generated shots never match the camera.
steps.does: Sets the look of each sequence and the rules that make generated and camera shots sit together.

steps.name: Titles and credits
steps.problem: Credits are typed at the last minute, and names are wrong or missing.
steps.does: Writes the main title design brief and the credit order from the brief, cast and crew.

steps.name: Lock, grade and delivery
steps.problem: A change arrives after picture lock. Conform, effects, sound and every version are redone by hand.
steps.does: Lists the versions a late change touches, and drafts the delivery trail for each AI shot.

steps.name: Release and marketing
steps.problem: The film is finished before anyone plans how people will find it.
steps.does: Plans the release: trailer beats, poster idea, loglines for each platform, festivals or channels, and a launch timeline.
